title: AI inference proxies gain named CISA KEV-timeline governance by Q2 2027
body: CISA's June 9 addition of CVE-2026-42271 - the unauthenticated command-injection flaw in LiteLLM's MCP-server preview endpoints, chainable with a Starlette host-header bypass into CVSS 10.0 remote code execution - to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog is the moment the agent stack's tool-wiring layer crossed from security research into a confirmed, in-the-wild, federally-tracked exposure with a remediation deadline attached. LiteLLM is the open-source proxy that brokers calls across hundreds of model providers, so the host that gets compromised is precisely the one holding every connected service's provider credentials and API keys; this is the same exposed surface the week's broader MCP wave keeps naming - the 67-CVE VIPER-MCP sweep, the roughly 40% of remote MCP servers with no authentication, the NSA design-considerations baseline, and the Ollama memory-leak flaw. A single KEV entry patches one CVE; it does not yet establish that the AI agent-broker and MCP-configuration tier is a distinct, governed software class. The forward thesis is that the US federal cyber-governance machinery formalizes that class: CISA promotes its handling of LLM proxies and MCP-config servers from case-by-case KEV listings into standing, named guidance or a binding operational directive that treats internet-reachable AI inference proxies and agent-tool brokers as managed, high-value-credential software - patch on KEV timelines, keep off the public internet, authenticate every caller. The concrete, falsifiable landing: by Q2 2027 CISA (or a joint CISA-NSA publication) issues binding-directive-grade or formally published guidance that names AI inference proxies, LLM gateways, or MCP servers as an in-scope category subject to KEV-timeline remediation and internet-exposure restriction - not merely additional individual CVE listings. If by June 30, 2027 the only federal action is further per-CVE KEV entries with no category-level directive or named guidance for the agent-broker tier, the prediction fails. The counter-risk is that CISA keeps the layer inside generic web-application and KEV processes and never carves out a named AI-agent-infrastructure class.

reasoning.because: CISA added the LiteLLM MCP-proxy RCE CVE-2026-42271 to KEV on June 9 as confirmed live exploitation
reasoning.given: the agent-broker/MCP-config tier is an unauthenticated, internet-reachable, credential-rich surface
reasoning.so_that: CISA elevates AI inference proxies and MCP servers from per-CVE KEV listings to a named, governed software class
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027: CISA named guidance scoping AI proxies for KEV timelines
reasoning.plain_language: After a US agency flagged a hacked AI proxy as actively attacked, it will likely write rules covering all such AI middlemen.

summary: CISA added the actively-exploited LiteLLM MCP-proxy RCE to its KEV catalog on June 9, putting a federal deadline on the layer that wires agents to tools. Expect CISA to move beyond per-CVE listings to named guidance scoping AI inference proxies and MCP servers as a governed class by Q2 2027.
